newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg faces easy Q2, Q3 comparisons - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg faces easy Q2, Q3 comparisons - analysts.

text.p: Kellogg Co, which as expected reported a 22 percent drop in earnings per share in the first quarter, will face easy comparisons for results in the second and third quarters, analysts said.
"I think the worse quarter is behind them. We can look forward now for a couple of up quarters...on very easy comparisons," Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said.
Still, Kellogg faces a challenge longer term to post continued stronger earnings, given the slow growth of the domestic ready-to-eat cereal market, analysts said.
"The domestic cereal category is still very problematic," Ghez said.
Kellogg shares rose 1-1/4 to 67-1/4, which analysts attributed to an outlook for improved near-term results.
"There may be a sense that the worst is over," BT Securities analyst John O'Neil said. "Starting next quarter, Kellogg should start generating earnings per share increases."

Kellogg said earlier it expects to show sales and earnings growth in the second quarter. In the second quarter of 1996, its sales dropped to $1.65 billion from $1.78 billion, and earnings before charges fell to $0.45 a share from $0.77.
While its second-quarter results likely will show improvement, it will be difficult for the company to match the $0.77 it earned in the 1995 period, analysts said.
"The company said it would be challenging to reach 1995 earnings levels" in the second quarter, O'Neil added.

Kellogg's third-quarter results this year will also face comparisons with depressed year-ago levels. In the third quarter of 1996, Kellogg reported earnings before charges of $0.85 a share, down from $1.05 a year before. Sales in that quarter dropped to $1.68 billion from $1.84 billion.
In the most recent quarter, Kellogg faced a difficult comparison as the first quarter of 1996 was the last period before the company reduced its prices.
The Battle Creek, Mich.-based company's 1997 first-quarter earnings fell to $0.77 a share from $0.99 in the year-earlier period. Sales fell to $1.69 billion from $1.79 billion.
Analysts said Kellogg's U.S. cereal volume fell two percent in the first quarter, although sales were helped by the launch of new cereals, Honey Crunch Corn Flakes and Cocoa Frosted Flakes.
International volume rose about two percent, less than expected, reflecting a cutback in retail inventories in Europe, analysts added.
Kellogg officials were not immediately available for comment.
